evidence_specificity.justification: Nearly every material claim has a specific file:line reference, and I verified ~20 of them against the actual source -- only 2 had minor off-by-one issues (bash-guard.sh:12 is actually line 11, bash-guard.sh:17-19 is actually 15-19). The jq gap analysis, bypass behavior, fail-open design, and dispatch mechanics all cite exact lines. The summary table of jq fallback coverage is particularly well-evidenced. Loses one point because the settings.json reference ('settings.json:8-106') was not verifiable in this grading pass, and a few claims about test assertion counts (~45, ~55, ~90+) use approximations rather than exact counts.

synthesis_quality.justification: The output builds a coherent narrative from registration (Layer 1) through platform bridge, dispatch, decision logic, bash guard, and post-write tracking (Layer 6). The flow diagram for write-lock decision logic is genuinely useful. Findings build on each other -- the jq fallback gap is introduced in the edge cases section, then threaded through the summary table, contradictions section, and deployment assessment. The bypass inconsistency analysis ('Wait -- is that a gap?') shows real-time reasoning that connects bash-guard and write-lock behaviors. Loses points because the IDE coverage matrix feels somewhat disconnected from the main narrative (mentioned but not deeply integrated), and the 'Contradictions and Tensions' section partially repeats findings already covered in Edge Cases.

efficiency.justification: The investigation is well-scoped to the question. Every major section serves the deployment readiness assessment. The end-to-end flow trace is necessary to answer the robustness question. However, some content is redundant: the jq governance marker gap is explained in Edge Case 1, then summarized again in Edge Case 3's table, then repeated in Contradictions, then again in Deployment Readiness -- four treatments of the same finding. The additionalContext injection (Edge Case 8) is relevant but low-priority for the deployment question. The BATON:COMPLETE filtering (Edge Case 6) is a minor detail that could have been a single sentence rather than its own subsection.

actionability.justification: The opening answer directly addresses 'is write-lock robust enough for team deployment?' with a clear yes-with-caveats. The deployment readiness section provides prioritized improvements (high/medium), specific code locations to fix, and concrete next steps. The 'What the Assessment Assumes' subsection is valuable for team deployment planning. Loses points because: (1) no risk severity matrix or likelihood assessment for the identified gaps, (2) no concrete implementation sketch for the awk fallback fix (just 'even a basic grep would be better'), (3) the Codex enforcement gap is noted but no recommendation is given for teams with Codex users beyond 'document it'.

improvement_suggestions: Consolidate the jq governance marker gap discussion into one definitive treatment rather than four partial mentions across Edge Cases, Summary Table, Contradictions, and Deployment sections
Add a concrete implementation sketch for the highest-priority fix (awk fallback for governance marker check) -- even 3-4 lines of pseudocode would increase actionability
Include a risk likelihood assessment alongside severity for each gap (e.g., 'jq missing is rare in practice but the impact is self-unlock'), so teams can make informed deployment decisions
Trim low-value edge cases (BATON:COMPLETE filtering, additionalContext injection) to single sentences within the flow trace rather than standalone subsections
